nodes.label: Linguaphone Russian Course
nodes.description: Linguaphone Institute Ltd. (London), mid-20th-century Soviet-era beginner conversational course: 30 illustrated lessons (family, home, meals, shopping, post office, doctor, tailor, radio, motoring) plus a 26-page grammar appendix with full declension/conjugation tables. Full 85-page extraction. Notably includes an explicit three-way regional dialectal note (мыза/хутор/заимка) and a pre-metric unit (аршин), both rare explicit region/register data points.

nodes.label: мыза/хутор/заимка — three-way regional synonym set for 'farmstead'
nodes.description: Linguaphone Lesson 19: the clearest explicit regional/dialectal naming note in this whole book — three regionally distinct synonyms for 'farmstead' (мыза in the western governorates, хутор in the south, заимка in Siberia), a genuinely load-bearing dialect-geography data point for this project's regional/geographic-scope fields.

nodes.label: аршин (archaic pre-metric unit of length)
nodes.description: Linguaphone Lesson 25 (tailor dialogue): 'Почём аршин?' (how much per arshin, ~0.71 m) — a pre-metric Russian unit still in commercial use in the period the course describes, direct evidence of period-specific measurement vocabulary worth preserving for historical/attested-era mechanics work.

nodes.label: Time-telling system (Lesson 6 worked examples)
nodes.description: Linguaphone Lesson 6: hours 1-12 disambiguated as day/night; minutes past the hour up to half-hour via '[N] минут(a) + [ordinal of next hour]' (пять минут первого = 12:05); minutes past half-hour via 'без [N] (минут) + [cardinal of next hour]'; 24-hour cardinal reading noted as common for train times specifically.

nodes.label: Verbal aspect (imperfective/perfective) as central difficulty
nodes.description: Linguaphone frames aspect as the central real difficulty of Russian verbs (no tense-for-tense English correspondence): imperfective has three tenses (incl. periphrastic future), perfective only two (its 'present-tense' form carries future meaning); worked желать/пожелать full paired conjugation across mood/participle/gerund; ~40-verb paired imperfective/perfective list with usage footnotes.

nodes.label: Six-case, three-declension noun system (hard/soft pairing)
nodes.description: Linguaphone grammar appendix: hard/soft vowel pairing (а/я, э/е, ы/и, о/ё, у/ю) as the master key halving declension-learning effort; six cases (incl. locative=prepositional, distinguished only by function); three noun declensions (feminine-only first; masc./fem. second; masc./neut. third), each hard or soft, with full worked paradigms for мать, комната, тётя, армия, стол, гость, попугай, кресло, море.

nodes.label: Long (attributive) vs. short (predicative) adjective forms
nodes.description: Linguaphone grammar appendix: long/full attributive form (красивый) vs. short/predicative form (красив, -а, -о, plural -ы for all genders), derived by cutting -ый/-ой from the masculine long form; also frames the pronoun он/она/оно declension as the historical basis of the long adjective ending.

nodes.label: Numeral government of noun/adjective case
nodes.description: Linguaphone grammar appendix: один(-type) + nominative singular; два/три/четыре + genitive singular (in nominative/accusative numeral position only, else full oblique plural); five-and-above + genitive plural; an adjective intervening between два/три/четыре and the noun goes to genitive *plural* (not singular) — flagged by the source as requiring particular attention; collective numerals двое/трое/четверо/пятеро given alongside cardinals.

nodes.label: The "golden rule" (velar/sibilant vowel restriction)
nodes.description: Linguaphone's own named term for the rule that г/к/х/ж/ч/ш/щ can never be directly followed by ы/я/ю (и/а/у substitute instead), presented as explaining apparent declension irregularities (книга→книги, not *книгы) as spelling artifacts rather than true exceptions.

nodes.label: The "to have" construction (у + genitive + есть)
nodes.description: Linguaphone: Russian has no principal verb 'to have'; possession is expressed as у + genitive-of-possessor + (есть) + nominative-of-possessed, есть dropped unless emphatic or interrogative (never dropped in questions); negation shifts есть→нет and the possessed noun to genitive (у меня нет книги).

nodes.label: The Russian case system (Prepositional/Accusative/Dative/Genitive/Instrumental)
nodes.description: Russian in Exercises Part II Basic Course: case-by-case chapters covering static-location в/на distinctions (lexically fixed per noun), personal-pronoun н-epithesis after prepositions, dative impersonal-experiencer constructions (мне трудно/легко/скучно/надо), genitive-of-negation and numeral-counting government, and instrumental sociative/predicate/passive-agent uses.

nodes.label: Verbs with the particle -ся (four functions)
nodes.description: Russian in Exercises: -ся verbs sorted into passive-like (Дверь открылась), middle-reflexive (умываться, садиться), reciprocal (познакомиться, встретиться), and lexicalized 'proper reflexive' (бояться, интересоваться, гордиться, several governing instrumental) — plus the orthogonal orientation-specific 'to put' triad класть/ставить/вешать.

nodes.label: Aspects of the verb (imperfective vs. perfective, full system)
nodes.description: Russian in Exercises: imperfective (names/progresses/repeats an action) vs. perfective (asserts completion/result); нача́ть/продолжа́ть/ко́нчить obligatorily take imperfective infinitive complements regardless of their own aspect; the three-way perception-verb split (видеть/увидеть, знать/узнать, слышать/услышать) between ongoing state and punctual 'become aware of' event, which English does not lexically mirror.
nodes.norm_label: aspects of the verb (imperfective vs. perfective, full system)

nodes.label: The complex sentence: subordination, conditionals, indirect speech
nodes.description: Russian in Exercises: interrogative-word subordinators; потому что/поэтому as mirror-image cause/result paraphrases; если-conditionals keeping plain future tense in both clauses (no English-style subjunctive shift); который relative clauses declining for gender/number by antecedent but case by their own clause-internal role; indirect-question word order with no partial inversion.
nodes.norm_label: the complex sentence: subordination, conditionals, indirect speech

nodes.label: Verbal adverbs / деепричастия (imperfective and perfective)
nodes.description: Russian in Exercises: invariable verbal adverbs describing an action by the same grammatical subject as the main verb — imperfective (-я/-а, simultaneous action) vs. perfective (-в/-вши, prior action) — valid as a subordinate-clause transform only when both clauses share the same subject, per the source's own explicit 'no replacement possible' exercise flag.

nodes.label: Participles (present/past active, complete/short-form passive)
nodes.description: Russian in Exercises: participles as declinable verbal adjectives standing in for a который-clause — present active (-ущий/-ющий, -ащий/-ящий, imperfective only), past active (-вший), complete-form passive participles (напи́санный, can carry a passive agent in the instrumental), and short-form passive participles (predicative-only, uninflected for case, mirroring the long/short-adjective distinction).

nodes.label: Verbs of motion: unprefixed pairs and directional prefixes
nodes.description: Russian in Exercises: идти/ходить and ехать/ездить unidirectional-vs-habitual contrast, with the past-tense trap (ходили = completed round trip vs. пошли = merely set off); a closed system of directional prefixes (при-, у-, в-, вы-, пере-, под-, от-, до-, про-, об-) attaching to these motion stems with fixed spatial meanings independent of aspect.
nodes.norm_label: verbs of motion: unprefixed pairs and directional prefixes

nodes.label: Russian in Exercises (Khavronina & Shirochenskaya)
nodes.description: S. A. Khavronina & A. I. Shirochenskaya, Russian in Exercises (Progress Publishers, Moscow, Soviet-era). Full-book extraction (172 scanned images, no text layer). Structured as Part I (Introductory Lexical/Grammatical Course, ~330-word core vocabulary) and Part II (case-by-case Basic Course: six cases, Verbs of Motion, -ся verbs, Aspect, Complex Sentence, Participles/Verbal Adverbs). A drill-heavy pedagogical companion rather than a narrative course.

nodes.label: Dative plural + age construction (Сколько ему лет?)
nodes.description: TYR Unit 10: dative plural endings for nouns/adjectives; age expressed via dative-of-person + a genitive-governed numeral (год/года/лет), with лет suppletively borrowed from an unrelated word (лето, 'summer'); days-of-the-week accusative (single occurrence) vs. dative plural (habitual, по + dative plural).
nodes.norm_label: dative plural + age construction (сколько ему лет?)

nodes.label: Future tense: imperfective vs. perfective
nodes.description: TYR Unit 11: compound imperfective future (быть-future + imperfective infinitive) for incomplete/repeated future action vs. perfective future (present-tense-shaped, from the perfective infinitive) for single completed future action; imperfective/perfective pair-formation strategies (prefix, ending-change, suppletion, motion-verb triads); давай(те) always + perfective future.

nodes.label: Weather constructions (verb/adverb/noun-based)
nodes.description: TYR Unit 11: three parallel ways Russian states weather — verb-based (идёт дождь/снег/град; светит солнце; дует ветер), adverb-based impersonal predicates (холодно/жарко/прохладно/душно/пасмурно/тепло, contrasted with agreeing-adjective 'погода жаркая'), and bare-noun statements (Сегодня туман).

nodes.label: Past tense formation and aspect in the past
nodes.description: TYR Unit 12: past tense built from infinitive minus -ть + л/ла/ло/ли agreeing in gender/number (not person); imperfective past (repeated/continuing/incomplete) vs. perfective past (single completed action); irregular past stems (вести→вёл, идти→шёл, мочь→мог, etc.); motion verbs' three possible pasts (habitual/round-trip, in-progress, perfective 'set off').
nodes.norm_label: past tense formation and aspect in the past

nodes.label: Dative-governing verbs (extended list)
nodes.description: TYR Unit 13 explicitly extends Unit 6's dative-governing verb list: звонить/позвонить, казаться/показаться, нравиться, помогать/помочь, рекомендовать/порекомендовать, советовать/посоветовать, хотеться/захотеться, plus dative time-phrases with к (к часу) and necessity constructions (Что мне делать?).

nodes.label: -овать/-евать and -казать verb conjugation classes
nodes.description: TYR Unit 13: -овать/-евать infinitives (рекомендовать→рекомендую) changing to -у- throughout the present, many loanwords (танцевать, нокаутировать); -казать verbs (сказать, заказать, показать) conjugating irregularly (скажу, скажешь...); includes болеть's two unrelated homographs (1st-conj. 'to be ill with' vs. defective 3rd-person-only 'to hurt').

nodes.label: Short-form adjectives for feeling/obligation (должен, нужен, болен, прав, жив)
nodes.description: TYR Unit 13: dative + short neuter adjective for how one feels (Мне жарко, Ему было плохо); short-form paradigms болен/должен/нужен/прав/жив each contrasted against a semantically distinct long form (больной, правый, живой); Russian's ban on possessive adjectives with body parts (у вас зуб, never 'your tooth').
nodes.norm_label: short-form adjectives for feeling/obligation (должен, нужен, болен, прав, жив)

nodes.label: хотеть (irregular verb 'to want')
nodes.description: TYR Unit 4: fully irregular paradigm я хочу, ты хочешь, он хочет, мы хотим, вы хотите, они хотят — a genuine conjugation-type switch mid-paradigm (1st-conj.-looking singular, 2nd-conj.-looking plural).

nodes.label: Russian plural noun formation (regular + irregular)
nodes.description: TYR Unit 4: hard/soft noun plural endings (-ы/-и, -а/-я), the г/к/х/ж/ч/ш/щ spelling rule barring ы/ю/я after these consonants, stress-shift-between-singular-and-plural, and a closed set of irregular/suppletive plurals (адрес→адреса, ребёнок→дети, брат→братья, друг→друзья, etc.).

nodes.label: Adjective agreement and endings (incl. какой)
nodes.description: TYR Unit 4: standard nominative adjective endings by gender, the г/к/х/ж/ч/ш/щ spelling-rule effect on adjective endings (-ий/-ие instead of -ый/-ые), the small 'stressed adjective' class (большой, молодой) taking -ой, and какой as both interrogative and exclamatory ('what a...!').

nodes.label: можно/нельзя/надо + bare infinitive
nodes.description: TYR Unit 4: the three core predicate words governing a bare infinitive — можно (permitted), нельзя (not permitted), надо (necessary) — e.g. В театре нельзя курить! Later units extend these into the dative-experiencer and past/future-tense systems.

nodes.label: «золотое кольцо» — Golden Ring (tourist-route epithet)
nodes.description: TYR Unit 5 reading text on Vladimir/Suzdal: 'золотое кольцо' names the historic Golden Ring tourist route of ancient Russian towns — a culturally load-bearing epithet illustrating figurative naming conventions applied to Russian places, alongside «мать русских городов» (Kiev) and «отец русских городов» (Novgorod, Unit 7).

nodes.label: The genitive case (introduction, singular formation, government)
nodes.description: TYR Unit 5: genitive as 'of'-case; required after quantity words (много, сколько, бутылка), certain prepositions (без, для, до, из, от, после, у), numerals 2-4 (genitive singular), and negative existentials (У вас нет билета); genitive singular endings by gender; genitive of personal pronouns identical to accusative; animate accusative = genitive singular.
nodes.norm_label: the genitive case (introduction, singular formation, government)

nodes.label: Третьяковская галерея (Tretyakov Gallery)
nodes.description: TYR Unit 6 reading text: the Tretyakov Gallery, founded by a rich 19th-century merchant (купец), illustrative cultural/historical vocabulary node (основатель, коллекция, живопись) anchoring the unit's museum/art vocabulary cluster.

nodes.label: The dative case (introduction, formation, uses)
nodes.description: TYR Unit 6: dative as indirect-object 'to/for' case; dative singular formation table; dative of personal pronouns; prepositions к and по governing dative; dative-experiencer impersonal constructions with можно/нельзя/надо/пора; the нравиться ('to please'=to like) and хочется ('feels like') dative-of-experiencer verb constructions.

nodes.label: этот/эта/это/эти demonstrative pronoun
nodes.description: TYR Unit 6: gender/number-agreeing demonstrative (этот университет, эта гостиница, это здание, эти театры); neuter это is formally identical to, but grammatically distinct from, the invariant particle это ('it is/this is').

nodes.label: Numerals, genitive plural, and case government by number
nodes.description: TYR Unit 7: numerals 20-1000 (no hyphens), compound-numeral noun-case agreement (ending in 1 = nominative singular, 2-4 = genitive singular), по + accusative for 'price per item', genitive plural formation for adjectives (-ых/-их) and nouns (fleeting-vowel insertion, gender-specific endings), and animate/inanimate accusative plural.
nodes.norm_label: numerals, genitive plural, and case government by number

nodes.label: Full declension of кто/что
nodes.description: TYR Unit 8 grammar point 8: full six-case declension of кто (кто/кого/кому/кем/о ком) and что (что/чего/чему/чем/о чём), given alongside the unit's instrumental-case material as the paradigm's completion.

nodes.label: The instrumental case (formation and uses)
nodes.description: TYR Unit 8: instrumental for means/instrument and profession ('to work as'), governed by с/перед/за/между/над/под/рядом с; singular/plural instrumental endings for nouns, adjectives, and personal pronouns; irregular instrumental plurals (людьми, детьми).

nodes.label: Short-form (predicative) adjectives
nodes.description: TYR Unit 8: short adjective forms (nominative only, predicative use) vs. long/attributive forms; рад flagged as the only common Russian adjective with no long form; fleeting-е insertion in the short masculine (вкусен, доволен, свободен, согласен); short neuter doubling as an adverb (быстрый→быстро); colour/nationality adjectives lack short forms.

nodes.label: Telling the time (Russian clock-time system)
nodes.description: TYR Unit 9: cardinal+час on the hour; minutes-past via genitive of the *next* ordinal hour (двадцать минут двенадцатого = 11:20); half-hour via пол- + genitive ordinal; minutes-to via без + genitive; a.m./p.m. disambiguated by ночи/утра/дня/вечера; 24-hour clock for timetables.

nodes.label: Paired motion verbs (habitual vs. one-direction)
nodes.description: TYR Unit 9: the habitual/multidirectional vs. single-occasion/one-direction motion-verb split (ходить/идти, ездить/ехать) plus the on-foot/by-transport split, extended to бегать/бежать, водить/вести, возить/везти, летать/лететь, носить/нести, плавать/плыть — each with its own present-tense paradigm, several irregular.

nodes.label: кайф / кайфовать
nodes.description: 'A high (feeling)' / 'to be high' — a well-known Russian slang borrowing (ultimately Arabic كيف via Turkic/southern-Russian contact); example sentence 'он кайфовал от выпитого' applies it to alcohol intoxication despite being introduced in the drugs subsection, evidence the word has broadened to general 'state of euphoria'.

nodes.label: хвост (academic sense)
nodes.description: 'An outstanding/incomplete exam, credit, or term paper' (lit. 'tail') — a body-part metaphor for unfinished academic obligations trailing behind a student; generates the collocation сдавать хвосты ('to make up outstanding work').

nodes.label: тачка (car, slang)
nodes.description: 'Car' (slang) — attested via a quoted 1994 «Спутник» magazine excerpt on car theft ('Продаётся «тачка» за 3-5 миллионов...'), where the source itself puts the word in quotation marks as a native-speaker slang-marking convention rather than an explicit (sl.) tag.

nodes.label: шпаргалка / шпора
nodes.description: 'Cheat sheet' — glossed by the source as 'заранее подготовленный письменный ответ' (a pre-prepared written answer); шпора is given as the clipped/informal variant of шпаргалка.

nodes.label: клёво (sl.)
nodes.description: 'Cool, great' — explicitly (sl.)-tagged, embedded in quoted in-group 1950s-60s стиляги dialogue ('...что-то у тебя получается не по-штатски'), doubly register-marked by both the tag and the surrounding slangy dialogue itself.

nodes.label: крутой (sl.)
nodes.description: 'Fantastic, great, terrific; tough' — source explicitly dates this: 'became very fashionable in the early 1990s', a rare item-level (not just book-level) era annotation.

nodes.label: чувиха
nodes.description: 'Girlfriend' — source explicitly dates this term to the 1950s and 1960s in its own footnote, one of only a handful of book-wide entries with an explicit era tag on the term itself rather than a coarse whole-book date.

nodes.label: кагэбэшник
nodes.description: 'KGB agent' (informal), built on the acronym КГБ + a colloquial -шник/-эшник person-noun suffix — glossed in-source as 'агент КГБ'.

nodes.label: сообразить на троих
nodes.description: 'To pool money for a bottle among three people' (lit. 'to figure it out among three') — the idiom encodes an entire culturally specific drinking-economy social protocol (finding two others, splitting cost evenly) compressed into one collocation.

nodes.label: штатник
nodes.description: A fan of everything American (lit. 'Statesman,' from 'the States'), an in-group self-designation coined by the стиляги-adjacent subculture, glossed in the source's running prose as 'поклонники всего американского'; same 1950s-60s milieu as стиляга/чувиха/клёво.

nodes.label: Soviet-era clipped/syllable-based compounding (медпункт, детдом, роддом...)
nodes.description: A productive Soviet-era word-formation pattern documented across multiple уроки: first syllable of one word fused with a second full/truncated word — медпункт, детдом, главврач (Урок 1), спецрейс, профсоюз (Урок 3, described there as a distinct 'truncated-first-root' compounding vs. full double-root compounding like всемирно/высококлассный), роддом (Урок 5). Confirmed across at least four chapters as a systematic, book-wide mechanism, not a one-off.

nodes.label: бэмвушка (BMW, informal)
nodes.description: An informal/affectionate car-name coinage from the brand acronym БМВ + colloquial suffix, from a 1990s dialogue ('Володя купил бэмвушку. — Какого года? — 93-го.'); parallels тачка as car-related slang and кагэбэшник as acronym-derived informal word-formation. Confirmed at 300 DPI re-render to resolve a borderline character.

nodes.label: Let's Talk About Life! (Tall & Vlasikova)
nodes.description: Emily Tall & Valentina Vlasikova, Let's Talk About Life! An Integrated Approach to Russian Conversation (Wiley, 1996). Proficiency-level (3rd/4th-year) conversation textbook, 9 thematic уроки (family/love, university life, rock music, alcohol/drugs, sexuality, religion, gender, social problems, Russia-and-the-West) plus Introduction and a whole-book Russian-English glossary (out of scope for this dispatch, but flagged as itself carrying (sl.)-tagged entries). Each уро́к supplies vocabulary, readings with footnoted register-marked vocabulary, taped-interview vocabulary, and recurring 'Word Study' root-family/word-formation boxes. All 053-053i split files (Урок 1 through Урок 9) constitute this ONE book.

nodes.label: Recurring cross-chapter bound-root 'Word Study' families
nodes.description: Every уро́к of this book (1 through 9) supplies a 'Word Study: Roots' box teaching a bound root and its derived-word family (e.g. держ- 'hold', ступ- 'step', тяг-/тяж- 'tight', мен- 'change', прет-/прещ- 'forbiddance', опас- 'danger') — a deliberate, systematic, cross-chapter morphological curriculum rather than nine disjoint vocabulary sets; several roots (ступ-, над-/на-, рав-) are explicitly recycled across multiple чапters' reading passages.

nodes.label: стиляга / стиляжка
nodes.description: Member of the 'stilyagi' — young Soviet people of the 1950s-60s who dressed in the latest fashion, influenced by Elvis Presley; source's own footnote gives an unusually full sociohistorical gloss (dress style, Elvis influence, decade range) rather than a bare translation. стиляжка is the diminutive.

nodes.label: самогон (варить, гнать)
nodes.description: Moonshine (to brew/distill) — source presents this as a widespread household practice ('во многих семьях гонят самогон'), not fringe; спирт (pure alcohol) is separately noted as sometimes drunk in Siberia specifically because 'он согревает' (it warms you), an explicit regional/climatic annotation.

nodes.label: 1950s-60s стиляги youth-subculture slang cluster
nodes.description: THE RICHEST DATED-SLANG FIND IN THIS CHUNK. Урок 9 Текст 1 (В. Аксёнов excerpt) footnotes stiляга/стиляжка, штатник, чувиха, and клёво all as belonging to 'молодёжь 50-х и 60-х годов' (youth of the 1950s-60s), explicitly tied to Elvis Presley's cultural influence and the in-group self-designation штатники ('fans of everything American'). Unusually precise item-level historical/sociolinguistic dating versus the book's typical coarse whole-book '1996' default — a genuine attested youth-subculture register cluster, cross-referenceable against any other mid-20th-c. Soviet youth-slang material found in other chunks of this project.

nodes.label: Address-replacing question openers (register-split: stranger vs. familiar)
nodes.description: §1: direct address is often replaced before a question by a fixed opener, sorted by register: stranger-directed (Простите, Извините, Простите пожалуйста) vs. familiar/junior-directed (Послушай(те), Слушай(те), Скажи(те)) — with the caveat that the familiar set is also used senior→junior regardless of prior acquaintance. Supported by Bulgakov/Lermontov/Pushkin excerpts.
nodes.norm_label: address-replacing question openers (register-split: stranger vs. familiar)

nodes.label: Negated yes/no question signalling hope or apprehension
nodes.description: §2: a yes/no question built with a negated verb (У вас нет сегодняшней газеты?) signals the speaker already leans toward expecting the positive state (hope) or fears an undesirable one (apprehension), contrasted against a genuinely neutral non-negated question; the same negated form can soften a request into politeness (Вы не скажете...?).
nodes.norm_label: negated yes/no question signalling hope or apprehension

nodes.label: Indirect ('relayed') questions with ли — strict word-order rule
nodes.description: §3: when relaying a question for the interlocutor to answer via a third party, ли must follow the predicate immediately if the predicate is fronted (не видел ли он Сашу), and is absent if the predicate is not fronted; ли in a *direct* question (predicate fronted) intensifies the hope/apprehension reading of §2. Extends beyond спросить/узнать to выяснить, уточнить, посмотреть, проверить, подумать/вспомнить (used reflexively).
nodes.norm_label: indirect ('relayed') questions with ли — strict word-order rule

nodes.label: The "X что" construction for checking a spontaneous guess
nodes.description: §5: что inserted directly after the noun/pronoun naming the person/thing a sudden guess concerns, never question-initial (Он что, ещё не вернулся?, not *Что он ещё не вернулся); illustrated across all three persons and animate/inanimate topics; an emphatic literary variant adds же (Вы что же...), drawn from Bulgakov and the Ирония судьбы screenplay.
nodes.norm_label: the "x что" construction for checking a spontaneous guess

nodes.label: А как об этом сказать? (Володина)
nodes.description: Г. И. Володина, А как об этом сказать? Специфические обороты разговорной речи [How to Say It: Specific Expressions of Colloquial Speech] (Moscow, Русский язык. Курсы, 2005/2003). Dedicated colloquial-pragmatics guide organized by conversational function rather than topic. This chunk covers only Раздел I.А 'Вопрос' §§1-5 (question-forming pragmatic constructions); later sections of the book are out of scope for this chunk.

nodes.label: Gendered marriage terminology (жениться vs. выйти замуж)
nodes.description: Урок 1: Russian lexicalizes 'get married'/'married-single' differently by the subject's gender — жениться/женат (of a man) vs. выйти замуж/замужем (of a woman) — with пожениться as the plural-only reciprocal for a couple. A lexical-semantic pattern foundational to any later gendered-register mechanics analysis.
nodes.norm_label: gendered marriage terminology (жениться vs. выити замуж)

nodes.label: Student jargon register (Из студенческого жаргона)
nodes.description: Урок 2 p.43, explicitly headed 'From student slang/jargon': засыпаться на экзамене / завалить-засыпать (кого) на экзамене (reflexive fail vs. transitive flunk-a-student, same root, agent/patient perspectives on one event), шпаргалка/шпора (cheat sheet), хвост (an outstanding exam/paper, lit. 'tail') and сдавать хвосты (to make up outstanding work). A tight, semantically coherent exam-failure micro-register.

nodes.label: Rock-scene colloquial/slang register (Урок 3 Диалог 5)
nodes.description: Урок 3's rock-music-scene dialogue, with the source's own inline (coll.)/(sl.) tags: классный (coll., 'great'), крутой (sl., source-dated 'became very fashionable in the early 1990s'), быть в отпаде (sl., 'to be ecstatic'), заумь (arcane/impenetrable lyrics, repurposing Russian Futurist 'zaum' poetics vocabulary), физтех (institutional-name clipping), Митрич (patronymic-clipped male address form).

nodes.label: Alcohol and drug slang register (Урок 4)
nodes.description: Урок 4's core vocabulary list itself parenthetically supplies slang synonyms next to neutral/clinical drug terms — марихуана (sl. травка, дурь), гашиш (sl. анаша), героин (sl. гера), морфий (sl. марфа) — the densest inline register-annotation in the book; plus кайф/кайфовать/ловить кайф (a Turkic/Arabic-origin loan broadened from drug-high to general euphoria, incl. alcohol), сообразить на троих (idiom encoding an entire three-way bottle-splitting social protocol), and мол (reportative/hearsay discourse particle).

nodes.label: Sexuality/reproduction terminology with explicit historical periodization
nodes.description: Урок 5: terms anchored to named historical thresholds supplied by the source itself — open discussion of секс dated to the glasnost period, absence of половое воспитание dated to до перестройки, гомосексуализм's decriminalization dated precisely to 1993 — unusually fine-grained Attested Era data versus the book's usual coarse 'contemporary (1996)' default.
nodes.norm_label: sexuality/reproduction terminology with explicit historical periodization

nodes.label: Practitioner/doctrine/adjective derivational triad (world religions)
nodes.description: Урок 6 p.141 'Религии мира' table: systematic three-column paradigm (practitioner noun / abstract doctrine noun / adjective) across six world religions/denominations, e.g. христианин/христианство/христианский; plus an explicit source footnote distinguishing еврей (ethnicity-primary, ordinary usage) from иудей (religion-practitioner-primary, source-flagged as rarely used) — a direct usage-frequency register annotation.

nodes.label: Gender-stereotype word-banks and self-directed word-formation exercise
nodes.description: Урок 7: gendered-labor-division word banks (сплетничать/воевать/драться/манипулировать vs. выносить мусор/стричь траву/содержать семью) for a discussion exercise; a self-directed Word Study (p.180) handing students complex derived words to decompose themselves, recurring the само-/все-/пуст- compounding families already documented in earlier chapters, plus a distinct native-root-vs-loanword layer contrast (эмиграция, эмансипированный, эгоистичный, цивилизация, парадокс).
nodes.norm_label: gender-stereotype word-banks and self-directed word-formation exercise

nodes.label: Crime-domain vocabulary and slang-marking conventions
nodes.description: Урок 8 Преступность subsection: core crime vocabulary (рэкет, вор, грабить/красть argument-structure contrast) plus a meta-level note that a dedicated dictionary of criminal-underworld jargon exists as a genre; тачка ('car', slang) is marked not via the book's usual (coll.)/(sl.) bracket-tag but via native-speaker guillemet-quoting inside a quoted 1994 magazine excerpt — a distinct register-marking mechanism worth separating from explicit ttextbook tags.

nodes.label: Early-1990s American-English loanword wave (Word Study: Americanisms in Russian)
nodes.description: Урок 9 p.242, explicitly framed by the source as a named sociolinguistic phenomenon ('one of the most striking features of the Russian language in the early 1990s'): 14 loanwords spanning pop culture (шоу, хит-парад), technology (софтвер, лэп-топ, дисплей), and post-Soviet economics (ваучер, холдинговая компания, спонсор), with бэмвушка (БМВ+suffix) as a two-layer borrowing-then-derivation case.
nodes.norm_label: early-1990s american-english loanword wave (word study: americanisms in russian)

nodes.label: Affective/expressive derivational suffixes (-яга, -ёныш)
nodes.description: Урок 9 Текст 2 footnotes name -яга as a colloquial expressive suffix (симпатяга 'likeable person', cross-referenced against бедняга/работяга) and -ёныш as marking 'the young of' something (вампирёныш, a coinage mocking Western children's-media monster characters). Both attach to already-meaningful roots for a colloquial/expressive register shift without denotational change.

nodes.label: Acronym+suffix informal-noun coinage pattern (-шник/-эшник)
nodes.description: кагэбэшник (КГБ + -шник = 'KGB agent, informal') and бэмвушка (БМВ + suffix = informal car name) form a small but real cross-chapter pattern of official-acronym-plus-colloquial-suffix coinage, sibling to тачка/рэкетир (Урок 8) as this book's recurring register-marking-via-derivation strategy — confirmed across at least three chapters' worth of independent examples.
